summary: The epicenter is the immutable Diagram revision model plus CanvasHistory and MappingDocumentController. Browser editing, agent commands, isolated generation, change proposals, and evaluations converge on these structures. Eleven selected points capture that shared core, its persistence boundary, and its principal consumers.

points.title: Immutable Diagram Model
points.rationale: Diagram combines versioned ASCII content, parsed nodes, source evidence, highlights, and jumps. Revision operations preserve logical node identities while validating edits. This is the fundamental value shared by rendering, agents, history, and storage; parser versions also protect existing node references.

points.title: Canvas Commands and History
points.rationale: CanvasHistory separates diagram revision bindings from composition, personal view state, and saved CanvasViews. MappingDocumentController applies version-checked semantic operations and coordinates checkpoints, alternatives, transfers, and navigation. Browser sessions and isolated server-side canvases reuse this boundary.

relationships.label: binds immutable revisions into canvas checkpoints

points.title: Interactive Canvas Editor
points.rationale: MappingPage assembles the workspace and command receivers. CanvasSession publishes committed state through focused stores, while the tldraw runtime owns live geometry and native undo navigation. Settled gestures become controller commands; rendering, selection, and routing derive from the same semantic document.

relationships.label: commits semantic edits and restores checkpoints
submits workspace changes and flushes acknowledged mutations
opens mapped source through repository services

points.title: Durable Canvas Persistence
points.rationale: Persistence separates immutable diagram/checkpoint records from mutable catalogs and workspace manifests. Browser-side change tracking sends record batches rather than complete histories. Server adapters validate versions and retry receipts, write referenced records first, and publish manifests or catalogs afterward.

relationships.label: stores and restores checkpoint graphs and workspace records
persists immutable revisions behind content-addressed references

points.title: HTTP and MCP Boundary
points.rationale: The Vite adapter exposes application services through HTTP, streaming responses, and live sockets. Bootstrap is the concrete composition root. The MCP server translates tool calls into these HTTP endpoints, making this the principal external access boundary rather than a separate implementation of canvas behavior.

relationships.label: dispatches canvas tools and attaches live readers
exposes chat and generation operations
serves source files and definition lookups
exposes workspace batches and canvas publication
exposes proposal workflows and push intake
exposes evaluation and comparison services

points.title: Live Canvas Agent Protocol
points.rationale: AgentDiagrammingSessionService binds tools to specific canvases and documents, validates requests, and manages retry-safe execution. Commands travel through a polling bridge to the browser; a separate live service distributes selection/context updates over sockets. Compact projections and revision guards keep agent references tied to the correct state.

relationships.label: dispatches bound browser commands and receives live state
redirects scoped reads and mutations into proposal sessions
uploads and resolves scoped agent context

points.title: Agent Chat and Generation
points.rationale: Agent Chat manages persistent conversations, native Codex events, tool bindings, and independent canvas alternatives. Diagram edit and batch services validate generated revisions before application. Codex stdio and Pi runtimes are distinct execution adapters; GenerationCanvasBridge gives child generations isolated controllers using the normal canvas command contract.

relationships.label: invokes canvas tools through bound sessions
creates isolated controllers for generated alternatives
validates and submits generated revision edits
reuses captured conversations and pinned source context

points.title: Reusable Agent Context
points.rationale: AgentContext captures immutable conversation trajectories and source constituents. The library adds durable identities, lineage, grouping, and retry-safe creation; transient uploads remain workspace/document scoped. Diagram-bound contexts and source snapshots make this a shared input boundary for edits, chat alternatives, and evaluations.

relationships.label: captures source ranges from registered corpus bindings
stores shared immutable source blobs
compiles contexts from diagram evidence and revision identity

points.title: Repository Evidence and Navigation
points.rationale: Source access resolves an explicit diagram or source binding rather than assuming one repository per project. Corpus providers handle filesystem reads, the repository registry handles Git identities, and optional language services resolve definitions. Browser repository and source panes consume this boundary to connect diagrams back to code.

relationships.label: resolves mappings, evidence, and source bindings
loads registered sources and saved representation bindings

points.title: Repository Change Proposals
points.rationale: ChangeSessionService captures repository-scoped canvases and Git hunks into isolated proposals, applies the shared controller operations, and retains baseline/proposed history for review. Acceptance checks captured versions before atomic catalog publication. DiffSession workflows and deduplicated push intake feed this same proposal lifecycle.

relationships.label: forks histories and applies shared controller operations
publishes accepted canvases and recovery receipts
uses agent tools during proposal materialization

points.title: Evaluation and Comparison Workflows
points.rationale: Evaluation runs pin prompt versions, contexts, and canvas checkpoints before generation. Materializers turn validated results into canvas outputs; comparison sessions preserve independent input copies. Experiments, judgements, and promotion build on these records, making this a substantial consumer of the shared model rather than a parallel diagram system.

relationships.label: pins and materializes independent canvas histories
loads immutable generation inputs
publishes promoted outputs into project catalogs
reconciles chat-generated alternatives into evaluation records
captures proposal sessions as evaluation outputs

limitations: Review depth varies. reviewedPaths includes files inspected through source declarations, imports, test names/assertions, or other excerpts; it does not mean every file was read in full. Central definitions and callers were traced in greater detail.

Many implementation and test bodies remain uninspected, particularly peripheral UI components, styles, benchmark/browser harnesses, migration scripts, projection-3d, and Python parser experiments. This is a global architectural assessment, not an exhaustive code audit.
The offline static-analysis subsystem and supporting tooling were considered but omitted from the selected epicenter. Their omission does not imply they are unused.

Assessment is limited to the working-tree snapshot captured at 2026-11-11T05:54:36.232538+00:00, based on head 8ca143700ca4d2c870f1101b8cd4601ab68abd41. Index exclusions include corpus, investigations, artifacts, generated stores/builds, vendor, node_modules, most documentation, binary/assets, and lockfiles.

No live repository, external sources, or existing diagram presentation was used to establish the architecture. Tests and runtime integrations were not executed; relationships reflect inspected source.
